plain_english: Time is divided by past and future; therefore, having rested in this limit of consciousness, one abides in a mere instant.
sanskrit_cite:
bhūtabhāvisvabhāvābhyāṃ sā hi yāti vibhāgitām /
tad asmin saṃvidavadhau viśramya tuṭimātrakam // [AgMsv_1.152]

plain_english: The yogin devoted to devouring time becomes a sky-mover in an instant; for time is the appearance of things, and that is of the nature of limitation.
sanskrit_cite:
kālagrāsaparo yogī jāyate khecaraḥ kṣaṇāt /
uktaṃ hi bhāvābhāso yaḥ kālaḥ sa kalanātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.153]

plain_english: Being and nonbeing are nothing other than the expansion of the rays of one's own consciousness; therefore, by stopping one's own rays, the whole sphere of paths is blocked.
sanskrit_cite:
svasaṃvidraśmisaṃsphāro bhāvābhāvaḥ sa nāparaḥ /
tasmāt svaraśmisaṃrodhadvāraruddhādhvamaṇḍalaḥ // [AgMsv_1.154]

plain_english: One who solely relishes the devouring of time becomes a sky-mover by himself; this is said by the Supreme Lord in the tantra called Śrīḍāmara.
sanskrit_cite:
kālagrāsaikarasiko jāyate khecaraḥ svayam /
tad uktaṃ parameśena tantre śrīḍāmarābhidhe // [AgMsv_1.155]

plain_english: Having restrained one's own circle of rays and drunk the unsurpassed nectar, one becomes happy in the present that is not limited by time or by both its extremes.
sanskrit_cite:
niruddhya raśmicakraṃ svaṃ pītvāmṛtam anuttamam /
kālobhayāparicchinne vartamāne sukhī bhavet // [AgMsv_1.156]

plain_english: Even restraint does not truly exist in that state free from contraction; and because of that absence, expansion does not exist either—so how could devouring and satisfaction exist there?
sanskrit_cite:
rodho 'pi nāma naitasmin saṃkocaparivarjite /
tadabhāvān na visphāro grāsatṛptī tathātra ke // [AgMsv_1.157]

plain_english: But by the method already described, restraint, expansion, devouring, and the rest do appear; yet from such appearance no other thing exists anywhere in the universe.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ tūktanītyā saṃrodhasphāragrāsādi bhāsate /
na tathābhāsanāc cānyad vastu viśvatra kiṃ cana // [AgMsv_1.158]

plain_english: Thus, enough of this extensive talk about the assembly of the khecarī circle; for in this teaching of Abhinavagupta, what yoga is there apart from the process of awareness?
sanskrit_cite:
ity alaṃ khecarīcakragoṣṭhyālāpena bhūyasā /
ko vābhinavagupte 'smin yogaḥ saṃvedanakrame // [AgMsv_1.159]

plain_english: Let us return to the topic: as far as the variegated consciousnesses emitted by the Goddess extend, so far above them is that higher and higher stream which is free from division.
sanskrit_cite:
prakṛtaṃ brūmahe devīvisṛṣṭāś citrasaṃvidaḥ /
yāvat tāvad tad ūrdhvordhvaṃ sroto yad bhedavarjitam // [AgMsv_1.160]

plain_english: From that stream arose scriptures such as the Saura and the Bhargaśikhā; and this is said in the Bhargaśikhā by the Supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite:
saurabhargaśikhādīni tataḥ śāstrāṇi tenire /
uktaṃ bhargaśikhāyāṃ ca devena parameṣṭhinā // [AgMsv_1.161]

plain_english: ‘O beloved, this knowledge born of the upper stream is that supreme knowledge’—so it is taught by that which expresses higher and higher forms of consciousness on the supreme path.
sanskrit_cite:
ūrdhvasrotodbhavaṃ jñānam idaṃ tat paramaṃ priye /
paramadhvaninordhvordhvasaṃvidrūpābhidhāyinā // [AgMsv_1.162]

plain_english: It indicated a distinction from the Siddhānta issued from the face of Īśāna; and even here there are variegations produced by the unmixed aspects of earlier divisions.
sanskrit_cite:
īśānavaktraniryātāt siddhāntād bhedam ādiśat /
atrāpi pūrvabhedāṃśavyāmiśrībhāvacitritāḥ // [AgMsv_1.163]

plain_english: Those various treasures of knowledge extend into diverse scriptural manifestations; but here the chief lineage of scriptures is sixfold in nature.
sanskrit_cite:
vijñānasaṃpadas tāṃs tāṃs tanvate śāstravibhramān /
iha yāvat tu mukhyeyaṃ ṣaḍātmā śāstrasaṃtatiḥ // [AgMsv_1.164]

plain_english: Those Trika scriptures that belong to the first half of this lineage are the ones the teachers have clearly spoken of under the name Ṣaḍardha.
sanskrit_cite:
etatpūrvārdhabhāgīni trikaśāstrāṇi yāni tu /
ṣaḍardhasaṃjñayā tāni gurubhir bhāṣitāny alam // [AgMsv_1.165]

plain_english: But this mode of expression is not used merely because the doctrine is deeply secret; for in that case, why could one not also say ‘half of half of twelve’ and so on?
sanskrit_cite:
na tu gūḍharahasyatvād evaiṣa vacanakramaḥ /
evaṃ hi dvādaśārdhārdham ityādy api na kiṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.166]

plain_english: Here the triad of powers is primary; it constitutes a complete abiding without mutual obstruction, full and of the nature of full consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
atra śaktitrayaṃ mukhyaṃ saṃpūrṇasthiti kalpate /
ananyonyoparodhena pūrṇaṃ pūrṇacidātmakam // [AgMsv_1.167]

plain_english: Beyond that, when in one power the triad takes on subordination and in another it partakes of subordination, that configuration is described as the yāmala.
sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ paraṃ tu tritayaṃ kasyāṃcid guṇitājuṣi /
anyasyāṃ guṇatābhāji yāmalaṃ paribhāṣyate // [AgMsv_1.168]

plain_english: Afterward, when the mass of objects has been emitted, through connection with the conditions of its variegation it appears in the five powers of one's own self, which are not divided into separate beings.
sanskrit_cite:
paścād visṛṣṭe 'rthaughe tadvaicitryopādhiyogataḥ /
pṛthagbhāvaviyogāsu svātmaśaktiṣu pañcasu // [AgMsv_1.169]

plain_english: In those five powers whose forms are consciousness, vibration, will, knowledge, and action, by the force of their own appropriateness and through the grace of the five Brahman-limbs, there arises what is born from the awareness of the flashing aspects of being.
sanskrit_cite:
citspandecchāvidākarmarūpāsu svaucitīvaśāt /
pañcabrahmāṅgasubhagāt sphuradbhāvāṃśabodhajam // [AgMsv_1.170]

plain_english: That form, having attained the nature of scripture, unfolds indeed in a fivefold way; for first there is the unfolding of the mass of beings situated within Ananta.
sanskrit_cite:
rūpaṃ śāstrātmatāṃ prāptaṃ pañcadhaiva vijṛmbhate /
tathā hi prāg anantāntaḥsthitabhāvaughajṛmbhaṇam // [AgMsv_1.171]

plain_english: As long as the Lord brings about that unfolding, there is abiding in the face of Īśa, in the unfolding of the inward, undivided power of action.
sanskrit_cite:
yāvat karoti bhagavāṃs tāvad īśamukhasthitiḥ /
antaḥsthāyā abhinnāyāḥ kriyāśakter vijṛmbhaṇe // [AgMsv_1.172]

plain_english: As it opens gradually, this expansion extends; and when the expansion of the power of action becomes clear, it will attain the state of māyā.
sanskrit_cite:
kramād unmiṣite tāvān eṣa sphāraḥ pratāyate /
kriyāśakteḥ sphuṭaḥ sphāro māyātvaṃ pratipatsyate // [AgMsv_1.173]

plain_english: In the own form of maya-tattva, it will be said of shiva and ishani as makers of pure, pure-other, impure universes.
sanskrit_cite:
māyātattvasvarūpe hi śiveśānīti vakṣyate /
śuddhaśuddhetarāśuddhaviśvanirmāṇakāriṇaḥ // [AgMsv_1.174]

plain_english: For the five-mantra-bodied shambhu, measurable impure association exists; indeed all is established at the prior extreme.
sanskrit_cite:
pañcamantratanoḥ śambhor nirmeyāśuddhasaṃgatiḥ /
asty eva pūrvakoṭyāṃ hi sarvam eva vyavasthitam // [AgMsv_1.175]

plain_english: Thus, for one wishing to go somewhere from his own house, at the first moment, whatever is to be gone, and the middle course, but.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi svagṛhāt kvāpi yiyāsoḥ prathamakṣaṇe /
yāvat kiṃ cana gantavyaṃ yac ca tanmadhyavṛtti tu // [AgMsv_1.176]

plain_english: Even at an instant's fall, all-knowing all-making power is gained from that for the steady skillful selves of special parts.
sanskrit_cite:
tuṭipāte 'pi sarvajñasarvakartṛtvalabdhṛtā /
tata eva viśeṣāṃśaniṣkampakuśalātmanām // [AgMsv_1.177]

plain_english: Thus, measured by birth-sword-edge touch, at the same time as shining, intellect draws forth special parts.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi jātyakhaḍgāgradhārāsaṃsparśasaṃmitā /
sphurattvasamakālaṃ dhīr viśeṣāṃśān prakarṣati // [AgMsv_1.178]

plain_english: The clear knower of jewel-tattva gathers those special parts seen like lightning, even among many jewels.
sanskrit_cite:
ratnatattvasphuṭaprajño vidyuttatkāladarśitān /
tāṃs tān viśeṣāṃś cinute ratnānāṃ bhūyasām api // [AgMsv_1.179]

plain_english: In the vina joined with many sound-material touches, variety is known in one expansion by one made of that.
sanskrit_cite:
anekasvarasaṃbhārasparśalāghavayojite /
vīṇāyām ekavistāre vaicitryaṃ vetti tanmayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.180]

plain_english: The hearing sense rested at the tip of dense practice stream indeed knows even that sound-part inner hearing less-more-ness.
sanskrit_cite:
nibiḍābhyāsadhārāgraviśrāntaśravaṇendriyaḥ /
vetty eva tatsvarāṃśāntaḥśrutyūnādhikatām api // [AgMsv_1.181]

plain_english: Let it be; in this nondifference doctrine, this succeeds effortlessly, where even in difference shining real nondual.
sanskrit_cite:
āstām abhedavāde 'sminn ayatnenaiva siddhyati /
etad yatra vibhāte 'pi bhede vāstavam advayam // [AgMsv_1.182]

plain_english: In difference-only-living scripture, this is clearly stood; for by Patanjali in the pada named powers.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedaikajīvite śāstre yāvad etad sthitaṃ sphuṭam /
tathā hi pātañjalinā pāde vaibhūtanāmani // [AgMsv_1.183]

plain_english: It was formed, 'from intuition or all'; here by me too, in intuition at first opening, consciousness-formed undivided.
sanskrit_cite:
nyarūpyata `prātibhād vā sarvam' atra mayāpi ca /
prātibhe prathamonmeṣe saṃvidrūpiṇy akhaṇḍite // [AgMsv_1.184]

plain_english: Thus the all-shining self, source of all accomplishment, stands in the created world, where creation is accepted by force.
sanskrit_cite:
sthitaḥ sarvasphurattātmā sarvasiddhiphalodayaḥ /
evaṃ jagati nirmeye nirmitsāsvīkṛtaṃ balāt // [AgMsv_1.185]

plain_english: Even impurity, fit for varied forms of that shape, appears in common form as a part beautiful as difference-self.
sanskrit_cite:
aśuddham api tadrūpanānāvaicitryayogy api /
sāmānyākārarūpeṇa dalaṃ bhedātmasundaram // [AgMsv_1.186]

plain_english: This difference-nondifference state stands bloomed; therefore it is in sadākhya, the nature of knowledge-power.
sanskrit_cite:
āste pronmiṣitaṃ saiṣā bhedābhedātmikā sthitiḥ /
ata eva hi sādākhye jñānaśaktisvarūpiṇi // [AgMsv_1.187]

plain_english: From impurity-particle-stain, state becomes higher-lower; even those reaching higher station arise from what is enjoyed by the lord.
sanskrit_cite:
aśuddhileśakāluṣyāt parāparatayā sthitiḥ /
teneśabhuktād etasmād apy ūrdhvapadabhāginaḥ // [AgMsv_1.188]

plain_english: From eagerness to manifest māyā, those enjoying its impressions thus receive various counsel full of many action-beginnings.
sanskrit_cite:
māyāprakaṭanautsukyāt tatsaṃskārajuṣas tathā /
bahukriyāsamārambhamayaṃ vividhamantraṇam // [AgMsv_1.189]

plain_english: Manifested from the great knowledge continuum and giving śiva, that state is there; another state is merged in the supreme state.
sanskrit_cite:
prādurbhūtaṃ mahājñānasantateś ca śivapradam /
sa hi tatrāparo bhāvaḥ parabhāvanimīlitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.190]

plain_english: But growth would not be attained in impure higher rite, like those fixed in other doctrines such as Vaiṣṇava and Buddhist.
sanskrit_cite:
na tu rūḍhim upāgacched aśuddhordhvavidhāv iva /
tena vaiṣṇavabauddhādiśāsanāntaraniṣṭhitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.191]

plain_english: As others are not properly liberated, so Śaiva-purified ones are not; they are in streams beyond path, order, triad, and others.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā samyaṅ na mucyante na tathā śaivasaṃskṛtāḥ /
atimārgakramakulatrikasrotontarādiṣu // [AgMsv_1.192]

plain_english: But for men properly initiated in the supreme lord's scripture, there is no difference at all in obtaining liberation.
sanskrit_cite:
parameśānaśāstre tu ye samyag dīkṣitā narāḥ /
teṣāṃ naivāpavargasya lābhe bhedo 'sti kaś cana // [AgMsv_1.193]

plain_english: Nor is there any means of liberation beyond this; only somewhere by effortless living-liberation order.
sanskrit_cite:
na caitadatirikto 'pi mokṣopāyo 'sti kaś cana /
kevalaṃ kvāpy anāyāsāj jīvanmuktikrameṇa ca // [AgMsv_1.194]

plain_english: Supreme accomplishment is indeed quick, as in our views; but somewhere, by the order of truth-series yoga, it comes only after long time.
sanskrit_cite:
śīghram eva parā siddhir yathāsmaddarśaneṣv iti /
kvāpi tattvāvalīyogaparipāṭīkramāc cirāt // [AgMsv_1.195]

plain_english: By those ritual parts the supreme fruit is obtained; therefore even here there is a kaulika view for destruction-seers.
sanskrit_cite:
tais taiḥ kriyākalāpaiś ca labhyate paramaṃ phalam /
ata evāsti saṃhāradṛśām kauliky apīha dṛk // [AgMsv_1.196]

plain_english: As stated, one should initiate dog-cookers at the beginning of time; the five consciousness-unfoldings formerly existed before difference.
sanskrit_cite:
yathoktaṃ kālapādādau dīkṣayec chvapacān iti /
cidunmeṣādikāḥ pañca yāḥ pūrvaṃ prāgabhedataḥ // [AgMsv_1.197]

plain_english: Declared in supreme Bhairava by union, those powers are differentiated through parts of being-limitation.
sanskrit_cite:
proktāḥ parasmiṃś cinnāthe bhairave samavāyataḥ /
tā eva bhāvopādhyaṃśalabdhabhedavibhāvitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.198]

plain_english: The difference-part alone is nourished, even by those enjoying before difference; thus rice-enjoyment nourishes the body.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedāṃśam eva puṣṇanti prāgabhedajuṣo 'py alam /
tathā hy odanasaṃbhogo yo dehasyopacāyakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.199]

plain_english: By phlegm accumulation that depletes the body; but even in god's world-self nondifference, from one's own fall.
sanskrit_cite:
kaphasaṃcayapātena sa dehasyāpacāyakaḥ /
nanu devasya viśvātmābhede 'pi svāparicyuteḥ // [AgMsv_1.200]

plain_english: Whence movement of capable limitations among changing things? Difference in Bhairava arises from being through that limitation-control.
sanskrit_cite:
vikāriṣv eva yogyānām upādhīnāṃ gatiḥ kutaḥ /
tadupādhivaśād bhedo bhairave bhāvasaṃbhavāt // [AgMsv_1.201]

plain_english: Thus it is not fitting to ascend our mind-ground; to say changing beings exist silently is indeed rashness.
sanskrit_cite:
iti nāsmanmanobhūmāv upāroḍhum ivārhati /
tūṣṇīṃ vikāriṇo bhāvāḥ santīti hy atisāhasam // [AgMsv_1.202]

plain_english: That god is indeed world-self and appears in such form; the undivided without limitation has divided limitation-appearance.
sanskrit_cite:
devaḥ sa eva viśvātmā tathārūpeṇa bhāsate /
anupādher abhinnasya bhinnam aupādhibhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.203]

plain_english: But thus that would be unreal; how is that very thing real? From such appearance, where is another real thing to be determined?
sanskrit_cite:
nanv itthaṃ tad asatyaṃ syāt kathaṃ satyaṃ tad eva hi /
tathāvabhāsanād anyat kva kiṃ satyaṃ nirūpyatām // [AgMsv_1.204]

plain_english: But thus is dream-world-cycle real? That indeed is devoid of desired action, unreal, yet conventionally used supremely.
sanskrit_cite:
nanv evaṃ svapnasaṃsāraḥ kiṃ satyaṃ kiṃtv asau kila /
abhīṣṭārthakriyāvandhyo 'satyo vyavahṛtaḥ param // [AgMsv_1.205]

plain_english: This is determined in detail ahead; therefore the unfolding power that was formerly undivided.
sanskrit_cite:
etac cāgre prapañcena yuktiyuktaṃ nirūpyate /
tasmād unmeṣaśaktir yā pūrvam āsīd abhedinī // [AgMsv_1.206]

plain_english: That being-unfolding nature has gone to that-person state; what is undivided is ungraspable, and what is grasping is the lord.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāvonmeṣasvarūpāsau yātā tatpuruṣasthitim /
yad abhinnaṃ tad agrāhyaṃ yac ca grāhakam īśvaram // [AgMsv_1.207]

plain_english: Now that standing is graspable from difference, its grasper of difference; called person, then declared from creation's beginning union.
sanskrit_cite:
adhunā tat sthitaṃ grāhyaṃ bhedāt tadgrāhakaṃ bhidaḥ /
puruṣākhyaṃ tataḥ proktaṃ sṛṣṭeḥ prārambhayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.208]

plain_english: From clear recognition the chief face is spoken; therefore here it destroys dispersion-being-state.
sanskrit_cite:
susphuṭapratyabhijñānān mukhyaṃ vaktraṃ ca bhaṇyate /
ata evātra visarabhāvasthitivighātakam // [AgMsv_1.209]

plain_english: Various disease-grasp aggregates and poisons are treated; many reasons split disease, calming and well-establishing.
sanskrit_cite:
nānāruggrahasaṃghātaviṣādi paricarcyate /
anekayuktidalitavyādhisaṃśāntasusthitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.210]

plain_english: Here beings that occur only in difference go to clarity; all being-ness indeed is this former-born face.
sanskrit_cite:
atra susphuṭatāṃ yānti bhāvā bhedaikavṛttayaḥ /
bhāvatvam eva yat sarvaṃ tat tv idaṃ pūrvajaṃ mukham // [AgMsv_1.211]

plain_english: From all and from excellence-rise, Ishana's upward-face-ness; in space-time-calculation void, not direction-difference imaginations.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvataś ca guṇotkarṣād īśānasyordhvavaktratā /
dikkālakalanāśūnye na tu digbhedakalpanāḥ // [AgMsv_1.212]

plain_english: Who indeed from which excellence-surpassing, thus upward will be; then beings when properly from desire-power.
sanskrit_cite:
yo hi yasmād guṇotkṛṣṭa iti cordhvo bhaviṣyati /
tato bhāvān yadā samyag icchatīcchāvibhūtitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.213]

plain_english: Ascended in that desire; if that desire is pure, by which through identity-union these touch consciousness-unity.
sanskrit_cite:
tadecchāyāṃ samārūḍhāḥ sā cecchā caiva nirmalā /
yena tanmayatāyogāt saṃvidaikyaṃ spṛśanty amī // [AgMsv_1.214]

plain_english: But beings hidden by limitation-superior desire-covering; then those beings stand, but god stands in own desire.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃtūpādhyuparaktecchāsaṃchādanatirohitāḥ /
te tadānīṃ sthitā bhāvā devas tu svaiṣaṇāsthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.215]

plain_english: One who knows only outer consciousness does not dwell in the supreme full state, so he appears as if in deep sleep.
sanskrit_cite:
parācīnitasaṃvittivaktro na ca parāṃ sthitim /
pūrṇām adhyuṣitas tena suṣupta iva bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.216]

plain_english: He is not truly asleep, for his sleep is only a closing; ultimate Bhairava-bliss consciousness never sleeps.
sanskrit_cite:
asuptaś ca prabuddhatvāt tasya svāpo nimīlanam /
na hy asti paramārthena bhairavānandasaṃvidaḥ // [AgMsv_1.217]

plain_english: When supreme light is present, where could closing shine except as its own measure?
sanskrit_cite:
tasmin paraprakāśe hi nimīlattvam upāgate /
pralayāt tannimīlattvamitir vā kutra bhāsatām // [AgMsv_1.218]

plain_english: No thing is unilluminated; even an imagined form shines in consciousness-light.
sanskrit_cite:
anābhātaṃ ca no vastu vyomasadmagavākṣavat /
so 'pi vā kalpitākāraś citprakāśe prakāśate // [AgMsv_1.219]

plain_english: This unblinking reality stands as if closing, for lords have unimaginable power that performs difficult things.
sanskrit_cite:
tad amīlita evāyaṃ nimīlann iva tiṣṭhati /
prabhūṇām avikalpyā hi śaktir durghaṭakāriṇām // [AgMsv_1.220]

plain_english: Some things happen with ease and some with difficulty; in this variety of appearance, he alone is autonomous.
sanskrit_cite:
idaṃ sukhena ghaṭate duḥkhena ghaṭate tv idaṃ /
ity ābhāsanavaicitrye svatantro hi sa eva naḥ // [AgMsv_1.221]

plain_english: His autonomy is the power called niyati; by it the bound soul is restrained and never finds autonomy.
sanskrit_cite:
tad eva tasya svātantryaṃ śaktir niyatināmikā /
yayā ruddhaḥ paśur jātu svātantryaṃ naiva vindati // [AgMsv_1.222]

plain_english: Because of dependence on that, difficult action is attributed to the lord; for the self of the universe nothing is easy or difficult.
sanskrit_cite:
tadapekṣābalāt proktā patyau durghaṭakāritā /
na hi viśvātmanaḥ kiṃ cit sughaṭaṃ vātha durghaṭam // [AgMsv_1.223]

plain_english: Why repeat this again and again when it is already established? Alas, for your forgetful nature, otherwise it would be useless.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ muhur muhur etenāsakṛn nanu nirūpitam /
hantāvismṛtiśīlaṃ tvāṃ praty etat syād apārthakam // [AgMsv_1.224]

plain_english: Effort aimed at one thing does not shine; rainy-season clouds do not arise for the prosperity of a single sprout.
sanskrit_cite:
ekam uddiśya kiṃtv etatsaṃrambho na virājate /
kiṃ hy ekāṅkurasaṃpattyai prāvṛṣeṇyāḥ payomucaḥ // [AgMsv_1.225]

plain_english: This is the vital spot here; the person to be instructed is pervaded in the heart-ground, drawn by a mass of action, through delicacy.
sanskrit_cite:
marmasthānam idaṃ cātra vyutpādyo hi janaḥ sa ca /
vyāpto hṛdbhuvi karmaughakṛṣṭāyāṃ saukumāryataḥ // [AgMsv_1.226]

plain_english: Endless sprouts and shoots rise from the maya seed, served by speech-fitness born of pride in difference.
sanskrit_cite:
māyābījotthitānantavikalpāṅkurakandalaiḥ /
bhedābhimānajanitavācanaucityasevitaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.227]

plain_english: As long as the great forest-fire of knowledge is not obtained, his duality grows again and again.
sanskrit_cite:
yāvad vidyāmahādāvajvālayaiṣā punaḥ punaḥ /
nālabdhā tāvad asyaitad dvaitaṃ rohet punaḥ punaḥ // [AgMsv_1.228]

plain_english: Split by sharp reason-axes kindled by true knowledge fire, the difference-tree never sprouts again.
sanskrit_cite:
tīkṣṇayuktikuṭhāraughaiḥ sadvidyāvahnidīpitaiḥ /
nirbhinno bhedaviṭapī punar naiva prarohati // [AgMsv_1.229]

plain_english: Even when god is seated in the deep-sleep portion, things go to false locality, like cavity and wood-apple.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ deve suṣuptāṃśamadhyāsīne sthitā api /
asaddeśīyatāṃ yānti bhāvāḥ śvabhrakapitthavat // [AgMsv_1.230]

plain_english: Here such own knowledge, laden with detachment, indescribable and unsupported, blooms by distinction.
sanskrit_cite:
atra tādṛśam eva svaṃ jñānaṃ vairāgyanirbharam /
nirupākhyaṃ nirālambaṃ vyajṛmbhata vibhāgataḥ // [AgMsv_1.231]

plain_english: Those ornamented with skull garlands, dwelling in cremation grounds, and perceiving element aggregates turn away from this.
sanskrit_cite:
kapālamālābharaṇāḥ śmaśānapadavāsinaḥ /
asmātparāṅmukhībhūtā bhūtasaṃghātagocarāḥ // [AgMsv_1.232]

plain_english: All enjoyable reaches the limit of disgust; the enjoyer is I. This body is only skin and bone, with no essence even in the smallest part.
sanskrit_cite:
bhogyaṃ jugupsāvadhi sarvam eva bhoktā hy ahaṃ kaḥ kila deha eṣaḥ /
carmāsthimātraṃ na ca sāram atra leśāṃśabhāge 'pi kadācid asti // [AgMsv_1.233]

plain_english: Thus practicing, they ascend the supreme wealth of detachment every moment and close, struck by that.
sanskrit_cite:
ittham abhyasyamānās te parāṃ vairāgyasampadam /
pratikṣaṇam upāruhya nimīlanti tadāhatāḥ // [AgMsv_1.234]

plain_english: Even sense-faculties rush toward suffering, yet mostly turn away from pleasure.
sanskrit_cite:
kim etad iti dhāvanti duḥkhe 'pīndriyavṛttayaḥ /
etad evam iti prāyo virajyante sukhād api // [AgMsv_1.235]

plain_english: With controlled mind, desirelessness toward seen and heard objects leads to desirelessness toward guṇas through knowledge of puruṣa.
sanskrit_cite:
dṛṣṭānuśravikārthaughavaitṛṣṇye vaśatādhiyaḥ /
tatparaṃ puruṣakhyāter guṇavaitṛṣṇyam ity api // [AgMsv_1.236]

plain_english: We ask, even without cause, what happens if anger does not arise, and what of the division-boundary.
sanskrit_cite:
nanv akāṇḍe 'pi pṛcchāmaḥ kiṃ cid yadi na kupyate /
* kim akāṇḍe bhedakāṇḍabhedakāṇḍaghaṭāvadhau // [AgMsv_1.237]

plain_english: If this consciousness is pure by nature, how does it exceedingly desire taste from impure enjoyments?
sanskrit_cite:
tarhi saṃvid iyaṃ śuddhā svabhāvād eva cet katham /
aśucibhyo 'pi bhogebhyo rasāt spṛhayatetarām // [AgMsv_1.238]

plain_english: Where has pride in the habit of non-forgetting gone now? Enough, or even this is said with intellect's reproaches.
sanskrit_cite:
nanv avismṛtiśīlatvābhimānaḥ kvādhunā gataḥ /
alaṃ vā buddhyupālabdhair uktam apy etad ucyate // [AgMsv_1.239]

plain_english: Consciousness is supremely real and luminous by nature; by union with world-illumination it appears, as explained.
sanskrit_cite:
svabhāvād eva saṃvittiḥ prakāśaparamārthikā /
viśvāvabhāsayogena bhātīti hi vipañcitam // [AgMsv_1.240]

plain_english: Therefore, in the world-circle of the consciousness-goddess, what arises from refutation in her rising within her own self?
sanskrit_cite:
ataś ca saṃvido devyā viśvasmin bhāvamaṇḍale /
svātmany evocchalattvaṃ kiṃ khaṇḍanādāyi jāyate // [AgMsv_1.241]

plain_english: Even when difference is manifested by the supreme lord's power, consciousness runs in beings and is distinguished.
sanskrit_cite:
yadāpi parameśānaśaktyā bhedo 'vabhāsyate /
tadāpi saṃvid bhāveṣu dhāvatīti vivicyate // [AgMsv_1.242]

plain_english: As the state of clod, pool, flame, breath, pot, and sky, so earth, ocean, great fire, wind, and infinite sky nature.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā loṣṭahradajvālāśvāsakumbhaviyatsthitiḥ /
dharāmbudhimahātejaḥsamīrānantakhātmatām // [AgMsv_1.243]

plain_english: This measure-formed consciousness, risen in itself, gradually follows beings of the same consciousness-formed class.
sanskrit_cite:
yāty eva mitirūpeyaṃ saṃvit svocchalitā kramāt /
saṃvidrūpasajātīyān bhāvān evānudhāvati // [AgMsv_1.244]

plain_english: Just as this was shaped by some supreme lord, who is able to set low pond-water in motion?
sanskrit_cite:
nyarūpyata tathā caitat kenāpi parameśinā /
nimnaṃ taḍāgapānīyaṃ kaḥ pravartayituṃ kṣamaḥ // [AgMsv_1.245]

plain_english: When that is full, streams flow in every direction; indeed, what and which ones flow thus by the force of their own nature?
sanskrit_cite:
paripūrṇe punas tasmin pravāhāḥ sarvatomukhāḥ /
nanu kiṃ kāṃś cid evetthaṃ saiṣā svaniyater balāt // [AgMsv_1.246]

plain_english: Thus that runs, and her body is the essence of attachment; there too only a reflection of attachment should be held.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ dhāvati tac cāsyā rāgatattvātmakaṃ vapuḥ /
tatrāpi ca tathā rāgābhāsa eva sa dhāryatām // [AgMsv_1.247]

plain_english: But let attachment exist in the conscious self, even of another color; if so, how indeed can she become detached anywhere?
sanskrit_cite:
cidātmani tu rāgo 'stu ko 'py anyārūṣaṇātmakaḥ /
nanv itthaṃ cet kathaṃ nāma sā kutrāpi virajyate // [AgMsv_1.248]

plain_english: Alas, this original argument has reached agreement: when consciousness itself is in a contracted state everywhere.
sanskrit_cite:
hanta prakṛta evāyaṃ vādaḥ saṃgatim āgataḥ /
yadā hi citir evaiṣā sarvataḥ saṃkucatsthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.249]

plain_english: Gradually from means of enjoyment, objects, and body, the enjoyer becomes empty like a part of great dissolution.
sanskrit_cite:
krameṇa bhogopāyebhyo bhogyebhyo dehato bhujaḥ /
bhogād bhoktus tathā śūnyā mahāpralayabhāg iva // [AgMsv_1.250]

plain_english: This destructive state arises in Rudra form because Sadyojata, Rudra, and Purusha are lord-natured.
sanskrit_cite:
jāyate rudrarūpaiṣā daśā sāṃhārikī yataḥ /
sadyojātaś ca yad rudraḥ puruṣaś ceśvarātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.251]

plain_english: Glorious Sadashiva, Deva, and Ishana are sung; Vishnu, Vama, Kajy, and Aghora will also be.
sanskrit_cite:
śrīmān sadāśivo deva īśānaś ceti gīyate /
viṣṇur vāmaḥ kajy aghora iti caitad bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_1.252]

plain_english: Because each has all power within, these Brahmas are called so by expansion, greatness, and universal expansion.
sanskrit_cite:
antaḥsthasarvaśaktitvenaikaikasyāpi bṛṃhaṇāt /
brahmāṇy etāni kathyante bṛhattvād viśvabṛṃhaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.253]

plain_english: Indeed, when other power is in excess and intended, each has a five-cause union.
sanskrit_cite:
tadanyaśaktyudrekāṃśe hy ata eva vivakṣite /
pratyekam asti brahmādihetupañcakayogitā // [AgMsv_1.254]

plain_english: That same power spreads distinctly in scriptures; therefore the primary fierce state stands in sadyojata.
sanskrit_cite:
saiva śāstreṣu bhedena teṣu teṣu pratanyate /
ataś ca sadyojāte 'smin mukhyā raudradaśā sthitā // [AgMsv_1.255]

plain_english: Even in contracted form it will be in consciousness expansion; the absorbed brahma and vishnu parts are forcibly lowered.
sanskrit_cite:
sā ca saṃkocarūpāpi cidvikāse bhaviṣyati /
yallīnau brahmaviṣṇvaṃśau tenādhaḥkurute balāt // [AgMsv_1.256]

plain_english: The state of absence of thing is the rudra presiding deity; it was described as a distinct object by Srimad Utpala.
sanskrit_cite:
vastvabhāvamayītyādidaśā rudrādhidevatā /
bhinnaprameyeti śrīmadutpalena nyarūpyata // [AgMsv_1.257]

plain_english: Even when born in mere distinction, contraction is approached; then enjoyer and enjoyed are clearly exchanged here.
sanskrit_cite:
jāto 'pi bhedatanmātre saṃkocaṃ yad upāgataḥ /
tato vyatinimīlete bhoktṛbhogyāv iha sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.258]

plain_english: That universe appears here immediately as if unborn; therefore the sadyojata term is of empty consciousness nature.
sanskrit_cite:
ajātam iva tad viśvam atra sadyo 'vabhāsate /
sadyojātapadaṃ tena śūnyasaṃvedanātmakam // [AgMsv_1.259]

plain_english: As long as he wishes to distinguish within the empty term, the god himself makes the universe rise, standing in awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ śūnyapadasyāntar yāvat sa ca vivikṣati /
devas tāvat svayaṃ bodhe viśvaṃ procchalati sthitam // [AgMsv_1.260]

plain_english: This expanding knowledge-power of the lord knows; absorption in the expanded consciousness abode is established for those two.
sanskrit_cite:
jānāti seyaṃ nāthasya jñānaśaktir vikāsinī /
tayor vikāsiciddhāmni līnatvam upapāditam // [AgMsv_1.259]

plain_english: The expansion of empty-form consciousness is indeed the universe; for it is full of deep sleep rest.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvidaḥ śūnyarūpāyā vikāso viśvam eva tat /
tathā hi ghanasauṣuptaviśrāntivaśanirbharaḥ // [AgMsv_1.262]

plain_english: Those house and shop parts called dream state are known; therefore that is not creation but maintenance.
sanskrit_cite:
tāṃs tān gṛhāpaṇādyaṃśān vetti svapnapadābhidhān /
ata eva na sā sṛṣṭiḥ sthitir eva tu sā tathā // [AgMsv_1.263]

plain_english: In previously created beings that is indeed mere consciousness; thus dream arises by distinction from waking form.
sanskrit_cite:
pūrvasṛṣṭeṣu bhāveṣu tad dhi vijñānamātrakam /
tathā ca jāgrato rūpāt svapno bhedena jāyate // [AgMsv_1.264]

plain_english: But the waking state and the others each have many divisions, which will be determined later; therefore it is fitting that their shining forth takes the form of emanation.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃtu jāgratpadādīnāṃ pratyekaṃ bahubhedatā /
nirṇeṣyate tato yuktaṃ sṛṣṭirūpeṇa bhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.265]

plain_english: Therefore, pervading those entities by his own awareness, the Lord causes that state of indifference of his to be abandoned through them.
sanskrit_cite:
ato nijavibodhena tān bhāvān vyāpnuvan vibhuḥ /
etais tyājayate tāṃ svām audāsīnyadaśāṃ vibhuḥ // [AgMsv_1.266]

plain_english: This is the expansion of the power of knowledge: entities abiding in the state of that knowledge attain fullness, with their own radiance unfolding.
sanskrit_cite:
jñānaśakter iyaṃ jṛmbhā tajjñānasthitibhāvinaḥ /
bhāvāḥ prayānti pūrṇatvaṃ vikāsinijatejasaḥ // [AgMsv_1.267]

plain_english: At the level of Sadyojāta there would indeed be supreme contraction, because firm abiding in their own nature does not arise for them.
sanskrit_cite:
paramaḥ khalu saṃkocaḥ sadyojātapade bhavet /
yad eṣāṃ svasvarūpasya niṣṭhā naiva sma jāyate // [AgMsv_1.268]

plain_english: Without rising into consciousness, how could distinctions like existence and nonexistence, inert and non-inert, or blue and non-blue ever be established?
sanskrit_cite:
vinā saṃvidupārohaṃ sattāsattā jaḍo 'jaḍaḥ /
anīlaṃ nīlam ityādivyavasthā kalpatāṃ katham // [AgMsv_1.269]

plain_english: As Utpalaguru said, just as the existent and the nonexistent have no intrinsic difference in their own nature, so too the inert and the non-inert do not; this is firmly established.
sanskrit_cite:
yad uvācotpalagurur yathā sadasatāṃ tathā /
jaḍājaḍānāṃ na svātmaviśeṣa iti niścitam // [AgMsv_1.270]

plain_english: Therefore, consciousness, in the fullness of its awareness, releases the states of self and other, and everywhere emits an animation of consciousness that is beautiful with bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmād bodhabharollāsavisṛṣṭasvaparasthitim /
cidanuprāṇanāṃ viṣvag vamann ānandasundarām // [AgMsv_1.271]

plain_english: That God, whose one body is consciousness, desiring to make the universe his own within the self of consciousness by emitting his own power of awareness, is called Vāma.
sanskrit_cite:
cidekavapuṣā viśvaṃ svīcikīrṣaṃś cidātmani /
svabodhaśaktivamanāt sa devo vāma ucyate // [AgMsv_1.272]

plain_english: Although, by the surge of his own power of awareness, this deity bestows such a form upon beings, nevertheless, in ultimate truth, the matter stands otherwise.
sanskrit_cite:
svabodhaśaktyudrekeṇa yady apy eṣa prayacchati /
bhāvānāṃ svavapus tādṛk tathāpi paramārthataḥ // [AgMsv_1.273]

plain_english: Desiring to take back these beings into himself, he constructs their divisions; therefore, in the arrangement of difference, this supreme lord is called Vāma.
sanskrit_cite:
svīkartum icchan saṃhāram eṣāṃ kalpayate bhidaḥ /
ato bhedavyavasthāyāṃ vāmo 'sau parameśvaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.274]

plain_english: Here such knowledge spreads; fortune is called the acceptance of distinct beings.
sanskrit_cite:
atra saubhāgyaniḥṣyandi tādṛg jñānaṃ pratāyate /
saubhāgyaṃ socyate teṣāṃ bhinnānāṃ svīkriyaiva yā // [AgMsv_1.275]

plain_english: Consciousness springs up from its own power and playful glimpse among varied beings.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāvānāṃ ca vicitrāṇāṃ bhogāṅgānāṃ svaśaktitaḥ /
svakautukakalālokād ucchalanty eva yā citiḥ // [AgMsv_1.276]

plain_english: That same consciousness colors the universe by nature, since manifestation is its own form.
sanskrit_cite:
saiva svabhāvarāgeṇa viśvaṃ rañjayate yataḥ /
vyakto hi rañjayed viśvaṃ vyaktiś cāsya svarūpataḥ // [AgMsv_1.277]

plain_english: The risen state of acceptance-desire stands for a moment in ray-essence wealth with undivided mind.
sanskrit_cite:
yaiva procchalitāvasthā svīkārecchābharodayaḥ /
tadraśmisārasarvasve kṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭhaty ananyadhīḥ // [AgMsv_1.278]

plain_english: What does the yoga-knower not attract or manifest? Scripture says the uncolored does not color.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ nākarṣati kiṃ naiṣa ca bhāvayati yogavit /
tata evocyate śāstre nārakto rañjayed iti // [AgMsv_1.279]

plain_english: Desire, placed and goad-enclosed, should accomplish desires and yoke them into desires.
sanskrit_cite:
kāmasthaṃ kāmamadhyasthaṃ kāmāṅkuśapuṭīkṛtam /
kāmena sādhayet kāmān kāmaṃ kāmeṣu yojayet // [AgMsv_1.280]

plain_english: Desire is acceptance-desire; by covering union the desirer accomplishes the universe, because this is desire-principle.
sanskrit_cite:
kāmaḥ svīkartum icchaiva tadācchādanayogataḥ /
viśvaṃ sādhayate kāmī kāmatattvam idaṃ yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.281]

plain_english: Thus in the supreme self, steadiness is directly superimposed through the covering order of risen awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi parame svātmany adhyāsya sthairyam añjasā /
taducchalitasaṃbodhakalāsaṃchādanakramāt // [AgMsv_1.282]

plain_english: The universe appears as servant under the desire-goad; by inner accomplishment method, this is understood in its own rise.
sanskrit_cite:
viśvaṃ kāmāṅkuśādhīnaṃ kiṃkaratvena bhāsate /
adhyātmasiddhayā yuktyā tv anayaiva nijodaye // [AgMsv_1.283]

plain_english: Life-force pervades body and eightfold city, drawing the universe because desire-principle manifests.
sanskrit_cite:
prāṇaḥ puryaṣṭakaṃ dehaṃ vyāpya viśvaṃ prakarṣati /
tattvasya kāmatattvasya prakaṭīkriyayā yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.284]

plain_english: Whether this secret is manifested in siddha circles, god spreads from void-bliss as risen-natured.
sanskrit_cite:
siddhacakreṣv idaṃ gopyaṃ kiṃ vā na prakaṭīkṛtam /
śūnyānandāt prasṛtyaiva devaḥ procchalitātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.285]

plain_english: Present, the lord proceeds by unfolding his own powers where he desires to enter, because the lord is covered.
sanskrit_cite:
vartamāno nijāḥ śaktīr vikāsyaiva pravartate /
yatrāsya pravivikṣāsti yataś ca prāvṛtad vibhuḥ // [AgMsv_1.286]

plain_english: That being remains after raising all powers in itself; then the consciousness-natured god appears as if submerged.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvāḥ śaktīr asau bhāvaḥ svātmany udrecya vartate /
tataś cidātmako devo nyagbhūta iva bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.287]

plain_english: These arisen powers shine as opening, desire, knowledge, and action; therefore that being appears even though endowed with four.
sanskrit_cite:
udbhūtās tu vibhānty etāḥ pronmeṣecchāvidikriyāḥ /
ataś catuṣkayukto 'sau yady api pratibhāsate // [AgMsv_1.288]

plain_english: Nevertheless, how could power-counting be real for it? Here only the art of uprooting parts of being-difference exists.
sanskrit_cite:
tathāpi śaktigaṇanā vastuto 'sya bhavet kutaḥ /
atraiva bhāvabhedāṃśanirmūlanakalā yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.289]

plain_english: Then conduct standing beyond world range occurs; from infinite power variety, uprooting and similar acts occur here too.
sanskrit_cite:
sthitas tataḥ samācāro lokātikrāntagocaraḥ /
anantaśaktivaicitryād atrāpy uccāṭanādayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.290]

plain_english: Even dissolution-play-predominant actions are established thus at the end of knowledge-power, with beings' body established.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃhāralīlābhūyiṣṭhā api tās tāḥ kriyāḥ sthitāḥ /
tad itthaṃ jñānaśaktyante bhāvānāṃ vapuṣi sthite // [AgMsv_1.291]

plain_english: Then final action-power respectfully withdraws them, as the most subtle power called opening at the supreme limit.
sanskrit_cite:
kriyāśaktir athāntyaiva tān saṃharati sādaram /
yathā sūkṣmatamā śaktir unmeṣākhyā parāvadhau // [AgMsv_1.292]

plain_english: By created being grossness it appears as gross form; thus this action-power is that in which beings are closed.
sanskrit_cite:
sraṣṭavyabhāvasthaulyena sthūlākāreva bhāsate /
tathaivaiṣā kriyāśaktir yasyāṃ bhāvā nimeṣitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.293]

plain_english: Some power established in its own form unfolds as if full; indeed there is action in which difference appears.
sanskrit_cite:
svasvarūpasthitā kāpi pūrṇeva pravijṛmbhate /
nanv asty eva kriyā yasyāṃ bhedaḥ pratyavabhāsate // [AgMsv_1.294]

plain_english: Not so: every action does not remove difference beforehand; thus on the ground of difference stand wood, fire, and rice.
sanskrit_cite:
maivaṃ sarvā kriyā bhedaṃ praty uta prāg vyapohati /
tathā hi bhedabhūmau ye kāṣṭhajvalanataṇḍulāḥ // [AgMsv_1.295]

plain_english: Those very things abandon difference in the state of cooking; if their natures were different, how could cooking unity arise?
sanskrit_cite:
ta eva pākāviṣṭatve bhedaṃ projjhanti sādaram /
yadi bhinnasvarūpās te pākaikyaṃ tat kathaṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.296]

plain_english: A different own-form of the parts is not reasonable; indeed cooking is not any thing that is many-formed.
sanskrit_cite:
bhinnaṃ svarūpam aṅgānāṃ na hi yuktyopapadyate /
nanu pāko na kaś cit sa yat tan nānāsvarūpakam // [AgMsv_1.297]

plain_english: Burning, moistening, burning and so on is called cooking; all different actions are established toward one fruit.
sanskrit_cite:
jvalanakledadāhādi tat pāka iti śabdyate /
bhinnā eva kriyāḥ sarvāḥ phalam ekaṃ prati sthitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.298]

plain_english: Cooking is said; no other action by name exists. How can many yield one desired fruit?
sanskrit_cite:
pāka ity ucyate nānyā kriyā nāmāsti kācana /
etad eva kathaṃ bahvya ekaṃ phalam abhīpsitam // [AgMsv_1.299]

plain_english: How would those accomplish it from the previously stated cause? Indeed, by eye, lamp, meaning, and mind-efforts, it is clearly so.
sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ saṃpādayeyus tāḥ. pūrvoktād eva hetutaḥ /
nanu locanadīpārthamanaskārair api sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.300]

plain_english: One knowledge is born; so here it will be. That is this body become dirty through kneading mud.
sanskrit_cite:
janyate jñānam ekaṃ tat tathaivātra bhaviṣyati /
